decisions: Package names: all 14 of the plan exist in Debian 13 amd64 under the same names; none changed.

Added, beyond the plan's list, because the slices' features do not work without them on a --no-install-recommends system: libpam-systemd (a logind session at login: S1 Lock/Suspend through the own session, polkit "active session" rules for udisks2 and NetworkManager, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and the user manager that starts PipeWire; neither the 13.0 base nor the 0.8.x set has it), wpasupplicant + wireless-regdb (NetworkManager cannot do Wi-Fi without wpasupplicant; it was only recommended), eject (udisks2 Drive.Eject runs it; S4 falls back to Eject when power-off is not offered), librsvg2-common (GTK3 needs the SVG icon loader for lxpolkit and LibreOffice gtk3), alsa-ucm-conf + alsa-topology-conf (laptop sound cards under PipeWire). polkitd comes as lxpolkit's dependency. Not added: dbus-user-session (the session uses dbus-run-session; it would change LS_XSESSION.sh's bus), rtkit, bubblewrap (the utility sandbox uses Landlock; bubblewrap is only its fallback), libreoffice-math, gstreamer1.0-gtk3.
K9's dbus-bin, S4's network-manager and x11-xserver-utils (xrandr) are already in the 0.8.x set. python3-pyatspi is kept because the plan lists it, though K7 said its reader does not need it.

LibreOffice stays at the 0.8.x set's 4:25.2.3-2+deb13u9 (Debian 13's point release; pinned in the private apt root), so the computer keeps one LibreOffice and the set holds no package twice. trixie-security has deb13u12; carrying it would mean the whole LibreOffice family again (~100 MB more) beside the old copies.

Owner model = Debian 13.0's required+important with dependencies (from snapshot.debian.org 20250810) + the 0.8.x set + the five base packages the 0.8.x set pins exactly (util-linux, systemd-sysv, fdisk, libfdisk1, liblastlog2-2), the most conservative system consistent with the 0.8.x set having installed. Three 13.0 base packages are upgraded by the new set (bsdutils, init, login).

PREPARE_DEBIAN.sh: skip a deb whose package is installed at the same or a newer version, and take the newest when the set holds a package twice. Reason: the set only grows, and on a Debian 13 installed or updated today the 0.8.7 script makes apt downgrade (11 packages on a fresh 13 install, 32 on an online-updated ThinkPad), which its --plan reports as resolved but the real -y install refuses. Also: a failed plan now shows apt's reasons (they were swallowed), and the final line says to log out and in.

INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh (the online route): --minimal-session also installs the 1.0 desktop packages; --calc/--math also libreoffice-writer, python3-uno, libreoffice-gtk3. The existing test's expectations (xserver-xorg xinit fluxbox in the line, exit 3) still hold.

Trust chain: Ubuntu's signed archive -> debian-archive-keyring 2023.4 (bookworm keys) -> trixie InRelease -> Debian's own debian-archive-keyring 2025.1 (trixie keys), then every index re-fetched and checked with it.
findings_for_the_coordinator: The 0.8.x set by itself does not install on an un-updated Debian 13.0: it upgrades libblkid1/libmount1/systemd but util-linux, systemd-sysv, fdisk, libfdisk1 and liblastlog2-2 pin them exactly and are not in the set. The owner's machine took it, so its base was newer; a new machine must be installed from a recent 13.x medium or updated first.

Three 0.8.x debs are no longer on deb.debian.org (base-files 13.8+deb13u7, libc6 2.41-12+deb13u4, firmware-amd-graphics 20250410-2: superseded by the 13.8 point release); fetched from snapshot.debian.org only for their control data, sha256 equal to the 0.8.x inventory. The owner's USB still has them.

On a ThinkPad whose LibreOffice was updated online (deb13u12), the set cannot add Writer/gtk3/python3-uno offline; the --plan now says why before anything changes, and the start page gives the online command.

S1's open question is answered by xsecurelock's own README in the Debian 13 package: "command line arguments following a \"--\" argument will be executed via execvp once locking is successful". Its PAM service is common-auth (no extra PAM file needed).

The PipeWire, pipewire-pulse and WirePlumber user units are enabled globally by their packages' postinst (deb-systemd-helper --user enable): with libpam-systemd they start at login, no PREPARE step needed. at-spi2-core starts through D-Bus activation (org.a11y.Bus.service), so it works on LS_XSESSION.sh's dbus-run-session bus; its Xsession.d QT_ACCESSIBILITY file does not run under startx (only matters for Qt programs).

native_sessions.py starts Calc with SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN=gen (no accessibility) and office_bridge.py uses svp: only LibreOffice started without these (program.open) shows itself to AT-SPI through libreoffice-gtk3.

R2: the new debs are in b100/R1/debs_new/ (largest file 9.85 MB, libreoffice-writer; every file is under 15,000,000 bytes); cut.sh copies OFFLINE_FILES.json/DEBIAN_USB.sha256 from the old kit and must take kit/ ones instead; the System set needs its own ZIPs of the 136 debs.
The registry and seed are untouched (no operations added).
not_done: Nothing was installed anywhere: the plan was resolved with apt-get -s against stand-in dpkg databases, and the installer ran only with --plan.
The 0.8.x debs were not downloaded; the rehearsal used stand-in files with their control data (what apt reads in a simulation).
Nothing ran on the ThinkPad, on real udisks2, PipeWire, logind, polkit, Wi-Fi or xsecurelock. Not tested in the owner's sense.
No ZIPs of the System set were cut (R2).
release_note: The 1.0 System set adds 136 Debian 13 packages (42.9 MB) beside the 0.8.x ones, nothing removed: USB drives (udisks2), the battery (upower), sound (PipeWire, WirePlumber), Wi-Fi (wpasupplicant), Lock (xsecurelock), the system's permission prompts (polkitd, lxpolkit), your login session (libpam-systemd), reading other programs (at-spi2-core, LibreOffice's GTK plugin), and LibreOffice Writer with its Python bridge. The installer now installs only what your computer does not have yet and leaves newer packages as they are; log out and in again afterwards. Built and resolved here against stand-in systems, not tested.
